text: [{"id":10,"latex":"We might try simply stipulating what desires the ideal observer has; for instance, that he is benevolent (desires the welfare of people in general).²⁶ One problem with this is that, in stipulating the ideal observer's motivations, we would simply be stipulating the content of moral theory. If we say, 'Ideal observers desire $x$, $y$, and $z$', then we are in effect stipulating that $x, y,$ and $z$ are the sole goods. This is because nothing else in the definition of the ideal observer entails any motivations, so the only things that all ideal observers would desire would be $x, y,$ and $z$. But then we might as well take the simpler theory, 'For a thing to be good is for it to be $x, y,$ or $z$', and call ourselves ethical naturalists. No work is done by adding the rest of the ideal-observer apparatus."}]
